content: 1. Osimertinib: Rifapentine reduces the plasma levels and efficacy of osimertinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Concomitant use with strong CYP3A inducers should be avoided. If unavoidable, close monitoring is required. 2. Ospemifene: Rifapentine decreases ospemifene levels by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2C9/10 enzymes. Use caution and monitor closely for reduced efficacy. 3. Oxybutynin: Rifapentine reduces oxybutynin levels via CYP3A4 induction. The clinical significance is unclear, but close monitoring is advised. 4. Oxycodone: Rifapentine decreases oxycodone levels by enhancing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for reduced analgesic effects. 5. Ozanimod: Rifapentine significantly reduces the exposure of ozanimod’s active metabolites (CC112273 and CC1084037) by inducing CYP2C8. Co-administration is not recommended due to potential loss of efficacy. 6. Paclitaxel: Rifapentine reduces paclitaxel levels and efficacy through CYP3A4 and CYP2C8 induction. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Pacritinib: Rifapentine decreases pacritinib levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 8. Palbociclib: Rifapentine reduces palbociclib plasma exposure by approximately 85% through CYP3A4 induction. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 9. Palovarotene: Rifapentine decreases palovarotene levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative therapy. 10. Panobinostat: Rifapentine reduces panobinostat levels by approximately 70% through CYP3A4 induction, leading to potential treatment failure. Co-administration is contraindicated. 11. Parecoxib: Rifapentine decreases parecoxib levels via CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 induction. The clinical significance is unclear, but close monitoring is recommended. 12. Pazopanib: Rifapentine reduces pazopanib levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Pemigatinib: Rifapentine decreases pemigatinib levels through CYP3A4 induction. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 14. Perampanel: Rifapentine reduces perampanel levels via CYP3A4 induction. Dose adjustments may be necessary if co-administered. 15. Pexidartinib: Rifapentine decreases pexidartinib levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 16. Phenytoin: Rifapentine reduces phenytoin levels by inducing CYP2C9/10. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Pimavanserin: Rifapentine decreases pimavanserin levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid co-administration if possible. Dose adjustments may be required. 18. Pimozide: Rifapentine reduces pimozide levels via CYP3A4 induction. The clinical significance is unclear, but close monitoring is advised. 19. Pioglitazone: Rifapentine decreases pioglitazone levels via CYP3A4 induction. The clinical significance is unclear. 20. Piroxicam: Rifapentine reduces piroxicam levels via CYP2C9/10 induction. The clinical significance is unclear. 21. Pirtobrutinib: Rifapentine decreases pirtobrutinib levels via CYP3A4 induction. If co-administration is unavoidable, dose adjustments are required. 22. Pitolisant: Rifapentine reduces pitolisant exposure by 50% via CYP3A4 induction. Dose adjustments are necessary, and monitoring is required. 23. Polatuzumab Vedotin: Rifapentine reduces the levels of unconjugated MMAE (a CYP3A4 substrate) derived from polatuzumab vedotin. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Pomalidomide: Rifapentine decreases pomalidomide levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 25. Ponatinib: Rifapentine reduces ponatinib levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid co-administration unless the benefits outweigh the risks. 26. Pralsetinib: Rifapentine decreases pralsetinib levels via CYP3A4 induction. If co-administration is unavoidable, double the pralsetinib dose starting on Day 7 of co-administration. 27. Praziquantel: Rifapentine reduces praziquantel levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 28. Prednisolone/Prednisone: Rifapentine reduces prednisolone and prednisone levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Pretomanid: Rifapentine decreases pretomanid levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers. 30. Primaquine: Rifapentine reduces primaquine levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Progesterone (Intravaginal Gel, Micronized, Natural): Rifapentine reduces progesterone levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use non-hormonal contraceptives as an alternative. 32. Propafenone: Rifapentine reduces propafenone levels via CYP3A4 induction. The clinical significance is unclear. 33. Propranolol: Rifapentine decreases propranolol levels by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Quazepam: Rifapentine reduces quazepam levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Quetiapine: Rifapentine decreases quetiapine levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Quinidine: Rifapentine reduces quinidine levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Quinine: Rifapentine decreases quinine levels via CYP3A4 induction. The clinical significance is unclear. 38. Quizartinib: Rifapentine reduces quizartinib levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 39. Rabeprazole: Rifapentine decreases rabeprazole levels via CYP3A4 induction. The clinical significance is unclear. 40. Ramelteon: Rifapentine reduces ramelteon levels via CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 induction. The clinical significance is unclear. 41. Ranolazine: Rifapentine decreases ranolazine levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 42. Regorafenib: Rifapentine reduces regorafenib levels and increases exposure to its active metabolite M-5 via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 43. Repaglinide: Rifapentine decreases repaglinide levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Repotrectinib: Rifapentine reduces repotrectinib levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 45. Ribociclib: Rifapentine decreases ribociclib levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Rifabutin: Rifapentine reduces rifabutin levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Rilpivirine: Rifapentine significantly reduces rilpivirine levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of virologic failure and resistance. 48. Rimegepant: Rifapentine decreases rimegepant levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 49. Riociguat: Rifapentine reduces riociguat levels via CYP3A4 induction. Dose adjustments may be required. 50. Ripretinib: Rifapentine decreases ripretinib levels and its active metabolite DP-5439 via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 51. Ritonavir: Rifapentine reduces ritonavir levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 52. Roflumilast: Rifapentine decreases roflumilast levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 53. Rolapitant: Rifapentine reduces rolapitant levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 54. Romidepsin: Rifapentine decreases romidepsin levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 55. Ruxolitinib (Systemic and Topical): Rifapentine reduces ruxolitinib levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Saxagliptin: Rifapentine decreases saxagliptin levels via CYP3A4 induction. The clinical significance is unclear. 57. Selexipag: Rifapentine reduces selexipag levels via CYP2C8 induction. Dose adjustments may be required. 58. Selpercatinib: Rifapentine decreases selpercatinib levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 59. Selumetinib: Rifapentine reduces selumetinib levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 60. Sildenafil: Rifapentine decreases sildenafil levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor closely. 61. Silodosin: Rifapentine reduces silodosin levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 62. Simvastatin: Rifapentine decreases simvastatin levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 63. Siponimod: Rifapentine reduces siponimod levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. This summary provides a detailed explanation of the interactions between rifapentine and various drugs, emphasizing the need for caution, monitoring, dose adjustments, or avoidance of co-administration where necessary.
